133: 		
134: 		if (!isClass(typeNode)) {
135: 			annotationNode.addError("@StandardException is only supported on a class");
136: 			return;
137: 		}

140: 		if (extending == null) {

142: 			return;

145: 		AccessLevel access = annotation.getInstance().access();
146: 		if (access == null) access = AccessLevel.PUBLIC;
147: 		if (access == AccessLevel.NONE) {

Fixed. The root cause: `@StandardException`'s generated no-args (`this(null, null)`) and message-only (`this(message, null)`) constructors pass untyped `null` literals, which become ambiguous during overload resolution when `@AllArgsConstructor` adds another two-reference-parameter constructor like `Failure(Date, Integer)`.

Changes (matching the upstream fix for lombok #3674):
- `src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleStandardException.java:162-172` — the no-args and msg-only constructors now cast the `null` arguments: `(String) null` / `(Throwable) null`.
- `src/core/lombok/eclipse/handlers/HandleStandardException.java:73-90` — same fix for the Eclipse (ecj) handler using `CastExpression` over the `NullLiteral`s.

Verification: `ant test.instance` (runs `lombok.transform.TestWithDelombok`) passes — 416 tests, 0 failures, including `javac-StandardExceptionWithConstructor.java` and `javac-StandardExceptions.java`, whose expected delombok output contains the casted `this((java.lang.String) null, (java.lang.Throwable) null)`.
